title: Break The Spin · Nov 20
subtitle: 6 posts, all real photos, no-fade layouts.

posts.quote: MUSK SPENT NEARLY $500 MILLION HELPING REPUBLICANS. NOW HE SAYS "I'M NOT MAGA." TRUMP FIRES BACK.
posts.alt: Two panels: a photo of Elon Musk on stage at CPAC in 2025 wearing a Make America Great Again hat and sunglasses on the left and an official portrait photo of President Donald Trump on the right. Bold text below reads: Musk spent nearly $500 million helping Republicans. Now he says "I'm not MAGA." Trump fires back.
posts.caption:
Elon Musk just broke with the movement he spent a fortune backing.

Speaking by video from China at the New York Times DealBook Summit, Musk was asked about the midterms, where he poured nearly $500 million into helping Republicans. "I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it," he said, before adding, "or maybe it would have been much worse without that."

Then came the line that lit up the internet. "I'm not MAGA," Musk said. "I'm not sure what MAGA means."

His biggest bet, $200 million against Democrat James Talarico in the Texas Senate race, failed. Talarico won. Musk even shrugged off Texas electing Democrat Gina Hinojosa as governor: "I don't think she's sort of a far-left governor," he said. "I think things will be fine in Texas."

President Trump answered on the way home from Asia. "MAGA, to me, means something very specific, and when people veer from it, they don't do very well," he told NBC News, before adding, "Elon's got very good intentions."
posts.first:
This is the same Musk who stood on the CPAC stage waving a chainsaw for DOGE less than two years ago.

Musk is free to call himself whatever he wants. But MAGA was never about one billionaire's checkbook. It was about secure borders, American jobs and a government that answers to the people who pay for it. Voters built that movement long before Musk wrote his first check, and they will be there long after he moves on.

Trump's answer was measured and fair. The movement does not need anyone's permission to exist, and it does not belong to the richest man in the room.

posts.quote: PAUL PELOSI HIT A PARKED CAR AND DROVE OFF. HIS JAIL TIME LASTED 36 MINUTES.
posts.alt: Booking photo of Paul Pelosi taken by the Napa County Sheriff's Office after his 2022 arrest. Bold text below reads: Paul Pelosi hit a parked car and drove off. His jail time lasted 36 minutes.
posts.caption:
Paul Pelosi, husband of former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, just served his jail sentence for a hit-and-run. It lasted 36 minutes.

According to the criminal complaint, the 86-year-old hit a parked, unoccupied Tesla on Yountville Cross Road in Napa County on July 3 and drove away. He was not charged with DUI. On November 3, he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor hit-and-run and an unlawful turn.

His plea deal: one year of probation, a six-month driver's license suspension, a 10-day work program, $11,191.14 in restitution to the car's owner, and one day in jail.

That one day turned out to be a little over half an hour. He reported to the Napa County jail on November 16. Records show he was booked at 10:28 a.m. and released at 11:04 a.m.
posts.first:
This isn't his first time behind the wheel in Napa County court. In May 2022, Pelosi was arrested after a DUI crash in Napa County. The photo above is the booking photo from that arrest. He got three years of probation.

To be fair, a misdemeanor hit-and-run with no injuries rarely means real jail time for anyone, and "one day" sentences are often served in hours. No statement from Pelosi or his attorney has been reported.

The restitution alone, $11,191.14, tells you how much damage was done to a car that was simply parked on the side of the road. But ask yourself how many ordinary Americans would get a deal like this on a second Napa County driving case. The rules always seem a little softer when your last name is Pelosi.

posts.quote: TRUMP JUST PARDONED PETE ROSE. NOW ONLY ONE THING STANDS BETWEEN THE HIT KING AND THE HALL OF FAME.
posts.alt: Photo of Pete Rose in a baseball cap. Bold text below reads: Trump just pardoned Pete Rose. Now only one thing stands between the Hit King and the Hall of Fame.
posts.caption:
President Trump just gave baseball's Hit King a pardon, more than two years after his death.

"I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND," Trump posted on Truth Social. He said Rose "was treated terribly by Major League Baseball in not allowing him to go into the Baseball Hall of Fame."

The pardon covers Rose's 1990 federal tax conviction. He admitted to filing false tax returns that left out nearly $355,000 in income, served five months in prison, paid a $50,000 fine, did 1,000 hours of community service and paid the IRS back more than $366,000.

Rose died in September 2024 at 83. Over 24 seasons, mostly with the Cincinnati Reds, he piled up baseball's all-time record of 4,256 hits, yet he has never been allowed into Cooperstown.
posts.first:
Rose agreed to a lifetime ban in 1989 after MLB found he bet on baseball. Commissioner Rob Manfred removed him from the permanently ineligible list after his death, which opened a narrow path. The earliest he could be considered is December 2027, by a 16-member committee, and he would need 12 votes.

Betting on baseball was wrong, and Rose paid for it for 35 years. But the game now partners with sportsbooks and runs gambling ads during broadcasts. Keeping the man with more hits than anyone in history out of the Hall of Fame looks less like principle every year.

Rose earned 4,256 hits on the field. It is time Cooperstown recognized it.

posts.quote: CHASE NOW SAYS COMPANIES IT WORKS WITH WERE HIT BY A CYBERATTACK. SOME CUSTOMERS' NAMES AND EMAILS MAY BE EXPOSED.
posts.alt: Two panels: a photo of a Chase bank branch storefront on the left and an official portrait photo of Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton on the right. Bold text below reads: Chase now says companies it works with were hit by a cyberattack. Some customers' names and emails may be exposed.
posts.caption:
After a week of outages, JPMorgan Chase has disclosed a cyberattack.

"We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack," Chase said on X. "Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors," which "may include some customer names and email addresses."

Chase says "there is no disruption to our services" and "there is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week," when thousands of customers could not log in or see their balances. The bank says it will contact affected customers and offer free credit monitoring. It did not name the vendors.

The disclosure came one day after Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told Congress the recent outages at the FAA, banks, the NSA and tech companies were not connected. "These are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes," Clayton said. "They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack."
posts.first:
Sen. Josh Hawley summed up how a lot of Americans feel about the official explanation: "That is quite a coincidence."

If you bank with Chase, watch for emails pretending to be from the bank. Stolen names and email addresses are exactly what scammers use for phishing. Do not click links in unexpected messages; log in through the app or type the address yourself.

The government says the outages are unrelated, and Chase says this attack is separate too. Maybe so. But Americans were told everything was routine maintenance, and now one of the biggest banks in the country is confirming a real cyberattack. People deserve the full picture, not one piece at a time.

posts.quote: RAVENS STAR MARLON HUMPHREY SAID BALTIMORE IS BEST AT MAKING CRIMINALS. HE APOLOGIZED. THE MAYOR: "A VERBAL APOLOGY IS NOT ENOUGH."
posts.alt: Two panels: a photo of Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey at training camp on the left and a photo of Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott on the right. Bold text below reads: Ravens star Marlon Humphrey said Baltimore is best at making criminals. He apologized. The mayor: "A verbal apology is not enough."
posts.caption:
One joke on a podcast just cost a Baltimore Ravens star a game.

On "The Marlon Humphrey Show," the Ravens cornerback was asked what Baltimore is best at making. He named "The Star-Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer. Then he added, "They're best at making criminals." The episode came down the same day.

Humphrey apologized to reporters after practice. "I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had yesterday to the City of Baltimore," he said.

That wasn't good enough for Democrat Mayor Brandon Scott. "A verbal apology is not enough," Scott wrote on Instagram, saying the city is full of young Black boys who look up to the Ravens. He wants to sit down with Humphrey in person.

The Ravens then made him inactive for their next game, against the Carolina Panthers. "This is about the team and putting us in the best position to be successful," coach Jesse Minter said.
posts.first:
Humphrey's line was a cheap shot, and he owned it fast. But notice what has the mayor fired up: a joke on a podcast.

Baltimore has had one of the highest homicide rates of any big city in America for years. Families there live with the reality of crime every day, not a punchline about it. If the mayor wants to sit down with someone, the people dealing with that reality deserve the first meeting.

An apology from a football player is easy to demand. Results on public safety are what Baltimore actually needs.

posts.quote: ONE YEAR AGO, VANCE LED RUBIO 54% TO 6%. NOW RUBIO LEADS THE 2028 GOP RACE 36% TO 20%.
posts.alt: Two panels: an official portrait photo of Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the left and an official portrait photo of Vice President JD Vance on the right. Bold text below reads: One year ago, Vance led Rubio 54% to 6%. Now Rubio leads the 2028 GOP race 36% to 20%.
posts.caption:
The 2028 Republican race just flipped.

A new Emerson College national poll has Secretary of State Marco Rubio leading Vice President JD Vance among Republican primary voters, 36% to 20%. One year ago, in Emerson's November 2025 poll, Vance led Rubio 54% to 6%.

That is a 46-point swing in twelve months. Ron DeSantis and President Trump each drew 7%, and 12% were undecided or picked someone else. Trump drew that 7% even though the Constitution bars him from a third term. The poll surveyed 1,000 voters from November 14 to 16, with a margin of error of plus or minus 3 points.

Rubio has spent the year as the face of the administration's foreign policy, from the war with Iran to the fight with the International Criminal Court. Vance has spent it taking fire from hawks over his criticism of "endless wars."
posts.first:
One poll is not a primary. Even Just the News notes the Emerson result could be an outlier, and the RealClearPolitics average shows a far closer race, with Rubio up by about a point and a half.

But the trend is hard to ignore. A year ago, Vance looked like the heir apparent. Now Republicans are openly debating who should carry the America First agenda forward, and Rubio has gone from an afterthought to the front-runner.

A single poll is a snapshot, not a verdict. The primary is more than two years away. That is a lifetime in politics, and both men will have plenty of chances to make their case.
